2609.16814.title: Can We Do Interpretable NLI with Graphs Based on Atomic Propositions?
2609.16814.paper_summary: While Large Language Model (LLM)-based Natural Language Inference (NLI) systems achieve high accuracy, their decision-making processes lack auditable structures. This paper explores whether NLI can be performed using only interpretable, graph-based representations of evidence. We introduce a fully graph-based pipeline where the classifier never directly processes the input text. Instead, sentences are decomposed into atomic propositions, converted into ConceptNet triples via constrained decoding, and represented as three graphs per pair: premise, hypothesis, and a retrieved ConceptNet subgraph. These graphs are then fed into a fine-tuned 0.8-billion-parameter language model. On the SNLI dataset, our pipeline achieves 89.7% accuracy, just 1.9 points below an identically trained text-based model. On ANLI, it matches the published performance of RoBERTa-large on rounds R2 and R3 (48.0% vs. 48.9% and 44.9% vs. 44.4%) but trails by 16 points on R1, resulting in an overall gap of 9 to 14 points compared to its text counterpart. We term this gap the price of interpretability and demonstrate that it stems from representational limitations rather than data constraints. Ablation studies further reveal that graphs and text are complementary: combining both modalities achieves 92.1% accuracy on SNLI.
2609.16814.paper_summary_zh: 雖然基於大型語言模型（LLM）的自然語言推理（NLI）系統達到了高準確率，但它們的決策過程缺乏可審計的結構。本文探討是否可以僅使用可解釋的基於圖的證據表示來執行NLI。我們介紹了一個完全基於圖的流程，其中分類器從不直接處理輸入文本。相反，句子被分解為原子命題，通過約束解碼轉換為ConceptNet三元組，並表示為每對三個圖：前提、假設和檢索的ConceptNet子圖。這些圖然後被輸入到一個經過微調的8億參數語言模型中。在SNLI數據集上，我們的流程達到了89.7%的準確率，僅比同樣訓練的基於文本的模型低1.9個百分點。在ANLI上，它與RoBERTa-large在R2和R3回合的已發表表現相匹配（48.0%對48.9%和44.9%對44.4%），但在R1上落後16個百分點，導致與其文本對應物相比，整體差距為9到14個百分點。我們將這一差距稱為可解釋性的代價，並證明它源於表徵限制而非數據限制。消融研究進一步顯示，圖和文本是互補的：結合這兩種模態在SNLI上達到了92.1%的準確率。
